L190: cite101†Learn more L191: ## What you will learn
L192: 
L193: Upon successful completion of this program, graduates will be able to:
L194:   * Provide person-centered care and assistance that recognizes and respects the uniqueness of each individual client.
L195:   * Use an informed problem-solving approach to provide care and assistance that promotes the physical, psychological, social, cognitive and spiritual health and well-being of clients and families.
L196:   * Provide person-centred care and assistance for clients experiencing complex health challenges.
L197:   * Provide person-centred care and assistance for clients experiencing cognitive and/or mental health challenges.
L198:   * Interact with other members of the healthcare team in ways that contribute to effective working relationships and the achievement of goals.
L199:   * Communicate clearly, accurately and sensitively with clients and families within a variety of community and facility contexts.
L200:   * Provide personal care and assistance in a safe, competent and organized manner.
L201:   * Recognize and respond to own self-development, learning and health enhancement needs.
L202:   * Perform the care-provider role in a reflective, responsible, accountable and professional manner.
L203: ## What to expect
L204: ### Program Duration and Maximum Time for Completion
L205: 
L206: The program is two years in length and divided into four terms.  The maximum time for completion is 5 years. Program completion deadlines are necessary to ensure the currency of student skills and in alignment with the BC Care Aide and Community Health Workers Registry recognition requirements.
L207: The program is divided into four terms. The theory component is delivered through class discussion groups, student presentations, lectures, online activities, demonstrations and guest speakers. Students apply the theory in the laboratory, clinical and practicum settings. Instruction in professional communication skills is provided throughout the program to support success in students' studies and the workplace.
L208: ## Admission requirements
L209: ### Program-specific
L210:   * Grade 12 graduation or equivalent
L211:   * Minimum 18 years of age
L212:   * English Language Proficiency as demonstrated by one of the following:
L213:     * Evidence of three years of full-time instruction in English and evidence of Grade 10 English with a minimum ‘C’ grade, or equivalent cite102†as specified by the BC Care Aid and Community Health Worker Registry L214:     * Evidence of less than three years of full-time instruction in English and evidence of required scores on a standardized English assessment cite102†as specified by the BC Care Aid and Community Health Worker Registry L215:   * Completion of the cite103†VCC Health Care Assistant Program English Competency Declaration form L216:   * A cite104†police check†www.canada.ca from the applicant’s country of origin, issued within 12 months before the program start date
L217: To be Completed During Term 1:
L218:   * Valid cite105†Standard First Aid and CPR-C certification L219:     * Certificate must remain valid throughout the program.
L220:   * cite106†BC FOODSAFE Certificate Level 1†www.foodsafe.ca L221:   * Criminal Record Check
L222:     * Students in this program are required to complete a CRC. The CRC must be completed according to cite107†VCC's Criminal Record Check instructions . Students whose CRC results indicate they pose a risk to vulnerable populations will not be able to complete the practice education requirements of the program or graduate.
L223:   * TB Screening
L224:     * Students must submit a negative tuberculosis (TB) skin test or chest X-ray dated a maximum of six months prior to the program start date. An additional TB test is required after each potential exposure to TB and/or travel to areas with a known prevalence of TB.
L225:   * Immunization Record
L226:     * A cite108†School of Health Sciences Student Immunization Record must be completed. Students may be declined placement in a clinical or practicum site if a completed immunization record is not provided.
L227:   * N95 Respiratory Mask
L228:     * An N95 respirator mask that is individually fitted by a trained provider, following CSA guidelines.
L229:     * The individual mask fitting should be done just prior to beginning the program. Mask fitting must be done annually. Students are responsible for the cost of the mask fitting.
L230:     * The original certificate must be presented to the department on the first day of class.
L231:     * See cite109†N95 Mask Fitting L232: ### General
L233:   * Seats are offered to applicants who have met all admission requirements, on a first-qualified, first-served basis.
L234:   * International applicants must be 17 years of age or older or a graduate of a secondary school. (Some exceptions may apply.)
L235:   * Applicants must submit cite39†official transcripts and educational documents as required by their course or program.
L236:   * All VCC applicants are required to function successfully in an English-speaking classroom. English requirements vary by program. For details, visit cite38†VCC International - English Requirements .
L237: ### Program Considerations
L238:   * Program tasks require extended periods (6+ hours) of standing/walking on concrete floors/hard surfaces.
L239:   * Program tasks can be physical demanding as they involve assisting clients with mobility, bathing and dressing.
L240:   * Program environment involves contact with latex-containing materials, including gloves, medical supplies, adhesives, and equipment.
L241:   * Program environment involves regular exposure to body fluids, strong odors, and situations where clients are partially or fully undressed.
L242:   * Program tasks require hand-eye coordination and dexterity. Activities may include instrument handling and technical work requiring steady hand movements (i.e.: cutting fingernails and brushing teeth).
L243:   * Travel to different locations in the Lower Mainland is required for clinical and community rotation requirements.
L244: ## Courses *
L245: 
L246: Classes are usually held from 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m., Monday to Thursday. Class times are subject to change.
L247: 
L248: This program includes off-campus practice education at health care sites primarily located in Burnaby, Vancouver and Richmond. As practice education involves day and evening shifts that can start at 6:30 a.m. or end at 10:00 p.m., students are encouraged to choose accommodations that are close to Skytrain stations to reduce the challenge of relying on early morning or night buses.
L249: ### Prior learning assessment and recognition
L250: 
L251: Prior learning assessment and recognition is not available for this program.

L203: cite126†Practical Nursing†www.youtube.com L204: ## What you will learn
L205: 
L206: Upon successful completion of this program, graduates will be able to:
L207:   * Apply the Entry Level Competencies for Licensed Practical Nurses (2021) to provide safe, competent, culturally safe and ethical care.
L208:   * Practice within relevant legislation, BCCNM Standards of Practice for LPNs Framework: Scope of Practice Standards; Professional Standards; and Practice Standards as set out by the Health Professions Act of British Columbia and the British Columbia College of Nurses & Midwives (BCCNM).
L209:   * Value and engage in continuous learning to maintain and enhance competence.
L210:   * Practice in collaboration with other members of the health care team to meet the collective needs of their clients.
L211:   * Participate in interprofessional problem solving and decision making processes.
L212:   * Advocate for and facilitate change reflecting evidence-informed practice.
L213:   * Make practice decisions that are client specific and consider client acuity, complexity, variability, and available resources.
L214:   * Use critical thinking, clinical judgment and knowledge of assessment to plan, implement, and evaluate the agreed upon plan of care.
L215:   * Develop a collaborative relationship with clients by connecting, sharing and exploring with them in a caring environment.
L216:   * Provide culturally safe, person-centered care across the lifespan that recognizes and respects the uniqueness of each individual and is sensitive to cultural safety, cultural humility and diversity.
L217:   * Provide leadership, direction, assignment, and supervision of unregulated care providers as appropriate.
L218:   * Identify one’s own values, biases, and assumptions on interactions with clients and other members of the health care team.
L219: ## What to expect
L220: ### Program Duration and Maximum Time for Completion
L221: 
L222: The Practical Nursing Diploma is sixteen (16) months in length. Students must complete the diploma within three (3) years from the initial start date to the completion date.
L223: This diploma program is offered on a full time basis and is divided into four levels. Each level must be successfully completed before the next one can be started. A major emphasis of this program is active student participation. Throughout the program the instructors will encourage the students to become increasingly more self directed and responsible for their own learning. Students are expected to come to class well prepared for active participation in classroom, nursing lab and clinical activities.
L224: Course guides provide direction of learning in preparation, in course activities and reflection of the content. The instructor acts as facilitator and expert to promote an environment conducive for learning through activities such as guided discussion, debate, audio-visual presentation, group activities, skill building exercises and simulation. Some courses may be offered in a blended delivery mode.
L225: Level one provides the foundation for the development of nursing practice and introduces the learner to the healthy adult.
L226: 
L227: Level two explores the older adult and concepts related to aging and chronic illness in various settings.
L228: 
L229: Level three examines a continuum of care in the community health setting and applies concepts from level one, two and three in the management of stable clients across the lifespan.
L230: Level four integrates knowledge from previous levels and examines concepts related to the care of the medical/surgical client.
L231: 
L232: Each level is supported by a Consolidated Practice Experience (CPE) which reinforces the learning that has taken place within each level.
L233: 
L234: Eligibility to enter the Consolidated Practice Experience at the end of each level is dependent upon the successful completion of all of the other courses within that level.
L235: Each level must be successfully completed before the next one can be attempted.
L236: 
L237: A final practice experience or preceptorship prepares the learner for the role and expectations of the graduate.
